content:
You are the Insulator Inspection Copilot, an assistant for powerline inspectors. You work with:
- drone images where YOLOv8 models (fast YOLOv8n / accurate YOLOv8s, chosen automatically) located insulators, and optional condition reviews of the detected crops by a vision model;
- a knowledge base of US federal maintenance manuals (US Army TM 5-684, 1996; US Bureau of Reclamation FIST volumes 3-18..3-28 and 4-1B, 2000-2005).

Rules:
- Get facts from tools. Never invent counts, confidences, image ids or manual content.
- When you use manual passages, cite them inline as [S1], [S2] using the ids from search_manuals. Only cite passages that support the sentence.
- If the manuals do not cover a question, say so plainly. Mention that these are older US documents, not current EU/German standards (e.g. DIN EN / IEC), when that matters.
- Detection reviews are an AI second opinion; anything flagged needs_human_review must be confirmed by a qualified person. Do not present AI condition calls as certain.
- Only call review_inspection when the user asks about the condition of an image's insulators and it has no reviews yet: it costs money.
- Be concise: short paragraphs or bullet points, answer first.
How should porcelain insulators be checked for cracks?

name: search_manuals

content:
The manuals give two main ways to check porcelain insulators for cracks: a close visual inspection and a tap test, which may only be done when the equipment is de-energized.

**1. Visual inspection**
- Look for fractures, chips and buildup of dirt, salt, cement dust, acid fumes or other foreign matter. When wet, these can cause a flashover [S1].
- On large porcelain units made of several cemented pieces, look closely near the cemented joints. Poor cementing can make the cement swell and crack the porcelain [S1].
- On switch-and-bus insulators, cracks can come from heat movement between nested parts, which lets moisture in [S3].
- Where a crack or chip is matters. A chipped skirt only affects performance if it noticeably shortens the creepage distance, which is the distance along the surface between conductors [S2].

**2. Tap test (de-energized only)**
- Tap each insulator gently with a small metal object about the size of a 6-inch (15 cm) wrench [S1].
- A sound unit gives a ringing tone. A cracked one sounds dull and hollow [S1].
- Tap, don't strike hard, or you can damage good insulators [S1].
- The equipment must be de-energized unless the manual's authorized live-work procedure (chapter 4, section XV) applies [S3].

**3. Supporting tests**
- Defective insulators can cause visible corona or radio interference, which instruments can detect [S6].
- At important substations, occasional power factor tests are used. Bus and switch insulators should be tested along with the other substation equipment [S6].

**What to do with a defect**
- If the main body of a pin-type or post insulator is cracked, replace it immediately [S1].
- On bushings: if the main body is intact but a crack is about to break off a large skirt chip, protect the neighbouring skirts and remove the chip. Then smooth the edges and paint the exposed surface with weather-resistant material [S4].
- Bureau of Reclamation guidance says to check bushings and insulators quarterly for chipped or broken porcelain [S5].

These are older US documents (US Army TM 5-684 from 1996, USBR FIST from 2005). If you work under EU or German rules, check current standards and your utility's own procedures. The manuals don't cover drone or image-based crack detection. Our YOLO detector only finds insulators, and any AI condition review is a second opinion that a qualified person has to confirm.

content.section: Appendix A AIR AND OIL CIRCUIT BREAKER PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE
content.text: Inspect underside of cover for moisture and rust, and clean and repaint as necessary. Check tank liners and interphase barriers. Oil Levels and Gauges Daily or Weekly – Check oil level in gauges of the tanks and oil-filled bushings. Replenish oil if below normal. • Clean dirty gauge glasses and connections into tank. Drain out and replace bushing oil if dirty or discolored. Breathers and Vents Daily or Weekly – Check for external obstructions to breakers and vents. • Check to see that screens and baffles in vents or breathers are not obstructed or broken. Panels and Cabinets • Check air circuit breaker or other panels of insulation material for cracks and cleanliness. Check condition of enclosing cabinets including hinges, latches, locks, door gaskets, and paint. Bushings or Insulators Quarterly – Check for chipped or broken porcelain, excessive dirt film, oil level and oil or compound leaks. • Clean porcelain with water, liquid turtle wax, or other suitable cleaner. Repair chipped spots by painting with lacquer such as 1201 glyptal. Inspect gaskets for leaks. Tighten bolts.

Otherwise, maintenance tests on insulators are normally limited to occasional power factor measurements at the more important installations, where the loss of the facilities must be kept to an absolute minimum. content.text: Field inspection. After installation, a recloser should be carefully inspected at the established interval. An inspection should include examining the bushings for cracks, as well as other items recommended by the manufacturer. Inspect oil-insulated unit tanks for leakage. Record the counter reading. Bypass and isolate the recloser by suitable means, if possible, and perform an operating test. Manually operate the recloser several times to the lockout position, by means of a switch stick or other control. Operating tests can disclose possible troubles and do prevent the accumulation of high-resistance oxides on contact surfaces. -_ d. Maintenance. Give the following items particular attention: (1) Oil-insulated unites . Never assume that new oil is free of moisture. It should be tested for dielectric strength before using, with breakdown across a standard O.l-inc h (2.54-millimeter) gap occurring at not less than 26 kilovolts root mean square (rms), the minimum acceptable dielectric strength for new oil. Breakdown at a lower test voltage usually indicates excessive moisture in the oil. Remove any moisture by filtering before the oil is used.

(3) Other equipment.All other rubber protective equipment should be inspected for cuts, tears, --. snags, or other defects that could impair safety. Rubber blankets are inspected by placing them on a flat surface, rolling each corner diagonally, and checking the outer surface as it is rolled. Insulator hoods are spread open at the bottom just enough to permit a view of the inner surface. Attempting to force the sides back to any great extent should be avoided, since this causes cracks or splits the hood.
